changes.after: Use a Go module from a local folder.

before: go.mod records the module path and Go language requirement. Imports use module paths, while package names are identifiers used in source. A module can contain several packages.

A require records a dependency version; replace can redirect that module to a local directory. Save the files below and run go run . with GOTOOLCHAIN=local and GOPROXY=off to prevent toolchain or dependency downloads. A replacement needs the local module’s own go.mod; it is not copied into the main module automatically.
```text
// go.mod
module example.test/app
go 1.27.0
require example.test/math v0.0.0
replace example.test/math => ./localmath
// localmath/go.mod
module example.test/math
go 1.27.0
// localmath/math.go (Go source)
package math
func Double(n int) int { return n * 2 }
```
Expected output or behavior: 12. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Change the local implementation and rebuild without fetching any external package. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A module is a group of Go packages managed together. Its go.mod file gives its module path and required Go version. An import uses a path to find a package; code uses the package name to call its functions.
A dependency is another module the program needs. `require` names its version. `replace` tells Go to use the localmath folder here. That folder needs its own go.mod file.
The screen shows `12`. main calls Double from the local math module, which multiplies 6 by 2.
Edit the local Double function and rebuild. The new program uses the changed local source. The replacement points to a folder; it does not freeze the old program.
